dedupe_keys.name: open flow based market coupling model on a test network

description: This is an open example model of flow-based market coupling, the method used to couple European day-ahead electricity markets while respecting grid limits, applied to a test network. It was released in December 2020 (version 1.0.0) by David Schönheit alongside the working paper "Toward understanding flow-based market coupling: An open-access model" by Schönheit, Kenis, Lorenz, Möst, Delarue and Bruninx. The test network is a modified version of the RWTH Aachen benchmark case for network expansion methods presented at IEEE PowerTech 2015, and renewable time series come from the EU EMHIRES data sets. The Julia code runs three stages: a two-days-ahead base case, day-ahead flow-based market coupling and intraday congestion management, with scenarios of higher renewable shares. Coverage is a stylised European-style test system, not a real grid. The code and documentation are accessible on GitHub and Zenodo under the GNU GPL version 3 at no cost. Caveats: it is a single release for teaching and research, and the network is a modified benchmark, not real data. Simulation uses are studying zonal market coupling, flow-based domain parameters and their effect on dispatch and congestion. Related records: model-open-tyndp covers European market and grid planning with open tools.
